preservationNote: All 107 research rows remain inventory; current shipped/partial/pending/retired status comes from Phase 28 and later executable evidence.

rows.capability: ACP core session lifecycle as a control plane (initialize, session/new, session/prompt, session/cancel, session/update, session/request_permission)
rows.rationale: impl/src/grok-acp.mjs drives the full ACP baseline against grok agent stdio: initialize handshake (protocolVersion 1), session/new spawn with cwd pinning, long-lived unbounded session/prompt as the turn, session/cancel interrupt (live-proven stopReason:'cancelled', session survives), session/update stream mapped to content.*, request_permission mapped to approve(). 8/8 live E2E verdicts. Driver-reachable via createDriver.

rows.capability: ACP session/load + session/resume (worker session resume without respawn)
rows.rationale: Researched and live-verified (loadSession capability advertised, sessions survive process kill and are session/load-able), but grok-acp.mjs never issues session/load — grep confirms zero occurrences. Every task pays a fresh spawn; a crashed worker's durable session is unrecoverable through the driver. Coordinator-restart persistence is fenced by docs/24 non-goals, but mid-run worker-session resume is not fenced anywhere.

rows.capability: ACP authenticate method / programmatic login (x.ai/auth get_url + submit_code, device auth)
rows.rationale: Adapter classifies the -32000 session/new auth gate as a typed spawn failure and stops; no programmatic authenticate flow. Quota-discipline constraint (creds presence-checked only) covers the testing posture but a headless fleet re-auth path is absent.

rows.capability: ACP bridge production patterns (orphan-result ledger, single-terminal-per-turn, keyed approval waits, anti-wedge auto-answer)
rows.rationale: The claude-agent-acp/codex-acp lessons landed as contracts: CS11 trailing-result discard and CS16 no-events-after-terminal (claude-session.mjs), X3 -32601 auto-answer for unmapped server requests + X4 keyed waits map (codex-appserver.mjs), GA16 terminalTurns set (grok-acp.mjs). Test-locked.

rows.capability: ACP _meta lossless side-channel consumption (per-turn usage telemetry)
rows.rationale: grok-acp.mjs maps the prompt response's _meta token accounting (totalTokens/input/output/cachedRead/reasoning/modelId) to resource.tokens{source:'promptMeta'} — the GA20 overturn, test-locked (F1).

rows.capability: Additional ACP vendor adapters (Gemini CLI --acp, Qwen Code, opencode acp, arbitrary agent_servers, PiCli)
rows.rationale: docs/24-goal-system-completion.md Non-goals: 'New vendor adapters (Gemini CLI ACP, Qwen Code, …) — matrix-documented, not adapter-built.' PiCli ships only as an honest-card placeholder in cli-adapters.mjs (spawn 'unsupported' until configured).

rows.capability: A2A five/six-state task lifecycle vocabulary (working, input_required, completed, failed, cancelled; immutable terminals)
rows.rationale: Adopted verbatim into coordinator.mjs task statuses per docs/08. Honesty note: TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES = {completed, failed} only, so result() on a cancelled task reports ready:false forever — a deviation from the researched immutable-terminal-cancelled semantics.

rows.capability: A2A input-required pause/resume semantic (ask primitive, fleet_respond)
rows.rationale: question.asked/approval.requested → task input_required + worker blocked; coordinator.respond(requestId, answer) resumes via adapter.answer()/approve() with single-consumer CAS and turn-epoch fencing (coordinator.mjs).

rows.capability: A2A refinements-as-new-tasks (refines / referenceTaskIds links)
rows.rationale: Task schema has deps[] for dependencies but no refines/referenceTaskIds link field; the researched refinement-lineage pattern (docs/08 'refinements are new tasks with refines: links') is absent. Low cost, low urgency for a single-box fleet.

rows.capability: A2A streaming/subscribe/status-artifact events (message-vs-artifact split)
rows.rationale: The pattern doc 03 recommended stealing is shipped as the in-process analog: append-only JSONL ledger + wait() digest with attention/facts split, and WorkerResult.artifacts kept distinct from content.message events.

rows.capability: A2A federation between hubs, remote fleet, foreman posture, AgentCard serialization
rows.rationale: docs/22 §5: 'Multi-machine / remote fleet, foreman posture, A2A federation, remote-control daemon + pairing — single box only.' docs/03: A2A is the designated inter-hub wire 'deferred until a second machine actually hurts.'

rows.capability: MCP northbound: hub-as-MCP-server, hub daemon, fleet_* tools, fleet_wait long-poll bridge, resumable wait cursors, fleet_review/bakeoff
rows.rationale: docs/24 Non-goals: 'MCP northbound (baton exposed as an MCP server to other agents) — phase-11 candidate; this goal is the southbound control plane.' Confirmed 0 occurrences in src (docs/22 §6 item 2). Baton ships as an in-process library; wait() + durable Cursor floors are the in-process analog of fleet_wait, already shipped.

rows.capability: MCP tasks extension mapping (tasks/get|update|cancel, notifications/tasks, task-augmented fleet verbs)
rows.rationale: The five-status vocabulary is shipped in the coordinator so the DAG is exposable 'with no translation' the day the northbound lands, but the northbound itself is the phase-11 fenced item (docs/24 Non-goals). Adoption timeline in host clients remains a tracked open question (docs/01 §3).

rows.capability: Harness-as-MCP-tool southbound (codex mcp-server, claude mcp serve)
rows.rationale: Researched and rejected on evidence: codex-runtime dossier §9 records that OpenAI's own plugin never uses it, the codex/event surface is slated for removal, and 'app-server is the only production control surface.' Baton drives app-server/stream-json/ACP instead.

rows.capability: Codex app-server session control plane (initialize handshake, thread/start, turn/start multi-turn, NDJSON framing without jsonrpc member)
rows.rationale: impl/src/codex-appserver.mjs: initialize{clientInfo} → initialized → thread/start{cwd, sandbox, approvalPolicy, ephemeral:true} → turn/start with renderBrief(brief,'codex-v2'); multi-turn via new turn/start per prompt. Protocol model verified FAITHFUL against the real 0.144.0 schema bundle (docs/23). Driver-reachable.

rows.capability: codex turn/steer (native mid-turn redirection with expectedTurnId precondition)
rows.rationale: prompt(mode:'steer') issues turn/steer{threadId, expectedTurnId, input}; live-verified mid-turn redirect and id-matched -32600 stale failure (docs/23 X1/X2). Reachable via coordinator.send(worker, msg, 'steer').

rows.capability: codex turn/interrupt with thread survival + 'then' follow-up
rows.rationale: turn/interrupt RPC; confirmed stop is exclusively the turn/completed status:'interrupted' event (XA8/D9); thread and child survive; interrupt(worker, then) auto-issues the follow-up as a new turn after confirmation (R5.1). Live-reproduced.

rows.capability: codex approval surface (commandExecution/fileChange requestApproval; accept/decline/cancel vocabulary; central answering)
rows.rationale: approve() maps allow→accept, deny→decline, cancel→cancel over a keyed waits map, answer-exactly-once (XA9/X4); item/tool/requestUserInput answered via answer() (first-question-only, documented MVP scope XA12). Unmapped requests (item/permissions/requestApproval, item/tool/call) auto-answered -32601 + observable error — safe under the driver's hardcoded approvalPolicy:'never' but would auto-decline legit escalations if a caller opened approvals via direct adapter.spawn.

rows.capability: codex per-thread sandbox/approvalPolicy configuration
rows.rationale: Adapter-only: spawn() honors opts.sandbox/opts.approvalPolicy on thread/start, but coordinator._dispatch only passes {worktreeReady, timeoutMs}, so through createDriver every thread runs workspace-write + approvalPolicy 'never' + ephemeral:true (ephemeral not overridable at all). Policy variation requires direct adapter calls.

rows.capability: codex thread/inject_items (native context injection)
rows.rationale: Researched as baton's context-injection primitive; the shipped nudge is an emulated in-adapter buffer (nudgeQueue, XA7) prepended to the next turn — grep confirms inject_items is never called. Native injection would make nudges land in model-visible history immediately instead of waiting for the next turn/start.

rows.capability: codex thread/resume, thread/fork, rejoin-running-thread semantics
rows.rationale: Heavily researched (resume precedence rules, fork lastTurnId truncation, rejoin as the daemon reattach primitive) but codex-appserver.mjs never calls thread/resume or thread/fork — the comment at line 11 acknowledges the protocol is 'designed for exactly that'. Combined with claude/grok this is the fleet-wide session-reuse gap: every task is a cold spawn, no branch-and-explore, no crash recovery of a live thread.

rows.capability: codex usage/rate-limit push telemetry (thread/tokenUsage/updated, account/rateLimits/updated)
rows.rationale: Both wire sources mapped to resource.tokens{source:'tokenUsage'|'rateLimit'} (XA18) and logged as digest facts. The consumption side is the budget-enforcement debt row.

rows.capability: Quota-aware scheduling (account/usage/read, rateLimits/read polling, usageLimitExceeded handling, claude usage_EXPERIMENTAL, time-aware/peak-hour dispatch, degrade-to-fewer-seats)
rows.rationale: Researched across all vendors (codex rateLimits snapshots, claude rate_limits utilization, GLM 3x peak multipliers) and designed into the harness-card/scheduler consequence in docs/01 §7 — but no proactive quota read, no time-aware dispatch, and no quota-driven seat reduction exists; only static concurrencyCeiling is enforced. Not fenced anywhere.

rows.capability: codex schema introspection for runtime feature detection (generate-json-schema diff, features list probing)
rows.rationale: Used as offline methodology (docs/23 verified the fake against the schema bundle) but the shipped card is static (verbs hardcoded, versionProbe = codex --version only); no schema-diff or features-list capability probe at construction, contradicting the interop doc's 'cards probed from installed binaries so they cannot drift'.

rows.capability: Harness-native goal pinning (codex thread/goal/set|get|clear, grok /goal command)
rows.rationale: Researched on both wires; unused by both adapters. The brief's definitionOfDone/verification pinned at spawn already keeps the done-definition outside the transcript, so the marginal value is a periodic re-assert (which the unbuilt governance firewall would own).
rows.researchedSource: docs/02 §Codex extras; docs/reference/grok-build-cli.md erratum #10; docs/24 preamble

rows.capability: codex remote PTY control (command/exec, process/spawn|writeStdin|kill|resizePty)
rows.rationale: docs/22 §5: 'PTY/tmux tier-3' correctly cut. The exec/process notification family is also in the adapter's documented silent-ignore table (XA17/D3).

rows.capability: codex remote-control daemon + pairing, cloud task submission, SSH foreman proxy topology
rows.rationale: docs/22 §5 defers 'remote-control daemon + pairing' with the whole multi-machine posture; single box only. The SSH-proxy foreman design is recorded for the fenced future.

rows.capability: codex shared-daemon/broker topology (unix-socket broker, single-flight -32001 contention, degrade-to-private-child fallback)
rows.rationale: docs/22 §4 planned '-32001 contention by falling back to a private child process'; the shipped adapter spawns one private child per worker unconditionally and treats -32001 during setup as a fatal typed failure, never retried (XA10). Works on a single box but wastes a process per worker and forfeits the researched OpenAI-plugin broker pattern. No fencing text found.

rows.capability: codex exec one-shot tier (exec --json typed events, exec resume, exec review)
rows.rationale: Adapter-only: CodexCli in cli-adapters.mjs (parseCodexEvent unit-tested against real captures, live-gated, kill native/interrupt emulated) — D1-conformant but not exported from index.mjs and never registered in any adapters map at HEAD. Expansion is explicitly fenced: docs/24 Non-goals 'One-shot tier expansion — G10 normalizes its card honesty; nothing more.'

rows.capability: Structured result contracts (codex --output-schema / turn outputSchema, claude outputFormat json_schema)
rows.rationale: Researched as native result-contract enforcement (doc 06 Q6) on both vendors; neither session adapter passes an output schema, and WorkerResult.summary is free text truncated at 500 chars. Would harden the trust-gate handoff and machine-readable progress. Not fenced.

rows.capability: Per-worker home/config isolation (CODEX_HOME, GROK_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; user-config bleed prevention)
rows.rationale: Live-proven hazard: grok ACP sessions connected the user's global MCP servers and ran settings.local hooks despite mcpServers:[] (erratum #9 — 'fleet workers must isolate with GROK_HOME'). No adapter sets an isolated home dir by default; callers can pass env but nothing derives the minimal config dir. A fleet worker inheriting operator hooks/MCP servers is a correctness and safety leak.

rows.capability: Cross-harness session migration (codex externalAgentConfig/detect|import, grok import)
rows.rationale: Researched on both vendors as roadmap-grade; no baton consumer and no obvious fleet need until resume itself ships. Not fenced.

rows.capability: Claude stream-json session control plane (dual-plane NDJSON, control_request/response, invocation constraints)
rows.rationale: impl/src/claude-session.mjs speaks the full researched protocol: --print --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose, persistent stdin, content+control planes, pendingControlRequests correlation, malformed-line tolerance, benign error responses for unknown control subtypes. Driver-reachable.

rows.capability: Claude native mid-turn steer (user frame absorbed at next tool boundary)
rows.rationale: The phase-8 flagship correction (CS7/E2): prompt(mode:'steer') writes the frame mid-turn with control.steer{midTurn} — no interrupt round-trip, no phantom events; live-proven ('REDIRECTED' single terminal). turn/nudge are wire-identical native frames.

rows.capability: Claude native interrupt (control_request subtype interrupt, <100ms, session survives, trailing-result discard)
rows.rationale: interrupt() sends the control_request, correlates the control_response, marks the in-flight turn's result frame for discard (CS11). Documented decline inside the row: the coordinator's `then` follow-up argument is dropped by this adapter (codex/grok honor it) — a small intra-fleet asymmetry. still_queued receipt is not consumed (no queued-message model in the adapter).

rows.capability: Claude interactive approvals (canUseTool via --permission-prompt-tool stdio; allow-with-updatedInput+toolUseID; deny; emulated cancel)
rows.rationale: approve() implements the E3 wedge fix (bare allow is silently re-asked forever); cancel emulated as deny+interrupt:true with emulated:true (D1 no-silent-emulation). Gated on constructor approvals:true, honestly carded 'unsupported' otherwise (CS18).

rows.capability: Claude MCP elicitation answering (question channel)
rows.rationale: answer() replies to elicitation control_requests with {action, content:{value}}; question.asked/question.answered wired through coordinator.respond(). Requires approvals:true.

rows.capability: Claude permission modes + print-mode auto-deny default fix
rows.rationale: E1: --permission-mode acceptEdits default (opt-out permissionMode:null) — the live-breaking auto-deny gap closed and live-proven. Full mode enum and mid-session setPermissionMode researched but only the spawn-time flag is used (mid-session reconfiguration is a separate debt row).

rows.capability: Worker session resume/fork through the driver (claude --resume/--fork-session/resumeSessionAt, codex thread/resume|fork, grok session/load + x.ai/session/fork)
rows.rationale: The resume/fork primitive is one of the researched ten; every vendor ships it natively and all three dossiers pin it live/doc-grade. Shipped reality: ClaudeSessionCli has a constructor-time sessionId→--resume only (adapter-only, coordinator never sets it); codex and grok adapters never call their resume verbs; the coordinator has no resume/fork command at all. Result: no worker crash-recovery, no session reuse across tasks, no fork-and-explore. docs/24 fences only coordinator-process persistence, not worker session resume.
rows.researchedSource: docs/02 capability matrix resume/fork row; all three vendor dossiers

rows.capability: Claude hooks surface for orchestration (30-event enum, PreToolUse input rewrite, PostToolUse output rewrite, stop-gate decision:block, --include-hook-events observation, CLAUDE_ENV_FILE)
rows.rationale: The deepest single research vein (two dossiers' worth) with zero shipped consumers: claude-session.mjs registers no hooks, passes no --include-hook-events, and the production-grade stop-gate template (codex plugin pattern) is unused. Per-tool-call policy enforcement stronger than approvals is available and unexploited. Not fenced; docs/02 called PreToolUse 'steering stronger than message injection'.

rows.capability: Claude inject-without-turn (SDKUserMessage shouldQuery:false, priority now|next|later)
rows.rationale: Researched as 'baton's inject primitive'; the shipped adapter has no append-context-without-turn path (nudge starts or joins a turn). Low priority because mid-turn steer covers most redirection needs; true inject matters for governance-firewall-style context refresh.

rows.capability: Mid-session reconfiguration (claude setModel/setPermissionMode/applyFlagSettings/setMcpPermissionModeOverride; codex sticky per-turn overrides)
rows.rationale: Researched on both wires; no coordinator verb exists to reconfigure a live worker (model, effort, permission mode). Workers keep spawn-time config for life. Not fenced; low urgency for probe-sized MVP tasks.

rows.capability: Compaction awareness + governance firewall (constraint re-injection on compact; compact_boundary/thread/compacted telemetry)
rows.rationale: Researched on both wires (claude compact_boundary with preserved anchor, codex thread/compacted) and designed in docs/21 ('compaction loses guardrails, not just objectives'); no adapter surfaces compaction events and nothing re-injects constraints/DoD afterward. Long-running workers silently lose their guardrails. Not fenced.

rows.capability: Claude control-plane introspection extras (getContextUsage, readFile, seedReadState, register_repo_root, mcp_call/mcp_message, dynamic MCP management)
rows.rationale: A large researched verb set with no shipped consumer. getContextUsage would feed the (also unbuilt) budget watchdog; the rest are conveniences. Not fenced.

rows.capability: File checkpointing / rollback (claude rewindFiles, grok x.ai/rewind/* snapshots)
rows.rationale: Researched on both vendors (grok is 'the only harness with true file-level rollback'); unused. Largely redundant in baton's architecture: workers run in disposable git worktrees and the trust gate snapshots via captureCommit, so rollback = discard the worktree.

rows.capability: Vendor-native multi-agent prior art (claude agent teams, --bg background agents, claude-squad, codex plugin broker/companion, stop-hook review gate)
rows.rationale: Studied as prior art to position baton, not as capabilities to ship: docs/01 §6 records agent-teams' 'single-vendor boundary is baton's reason to exist'; the broker/companion/stop-gate patterns were mined for contracts (X4, stop-gate template) rather than adopted wholesale. No doc proposes shipping them.

rows.capability: Claude adapter-as-daemon owning N children (per-process control asymmetry answer)
rows.rationale: The researched shape ('a small daemon owning N child processes') landed as the coordinator process itself: one ClaudeSessionCli child per worker inside one driver process. A standalone reattachable daemon is fenced with the MCP-northbound/hub-daemon non-goal (docs/24) and coordinator-persistence non-goal.

rows.capability: Claude reinitialize daemon-reattach primitive
rows.rationale: Researched as 'the reattach primitive baton doc 02 said Claude lacked', but its only baton use-case is surviving a coordinator/transport restart — docs/24 Non-goals: 'Coordinator persistence/resume across process restarts — out unless a confirmed gap forces it (none does).'

rows.capability: GLM harness via Claude Code + Z.ai Anthropic endpoint (env wiring, model mapping, ceiling 1)
rows.rationale: GlmSessionCli (claude-session.mjs subclass, SC6) driver-reachable and index-exported: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/AUTH_TOKEN from Z_AI_API_KEY/ZHIPU_API_KEY, model→OPUS/SONNET map env vars, harness 'glm-via-claude-session', concurrencyCeiling 1 derived from Z.ai Pro. Every session verb (steer/interrupt/approvals) inherited. One-shot ZCodeCli duplicate exists adapter-only.

rows.capability: GLM non-refuser capability tags + deterministic domain routing (SC7)
rows.rationale: card().nonRefuserFor defaults to ['ml-ai-inference-training','cybersecurity']; createDriver's route() restricts the feasible pool to capable vendors when taskType matches, feasibility-first so a saturated vendor never strands a task. Closes the G11 gap doc 24 recorded as open.
rows.researchedSource: docs/23 re-steer item 3; docs/24 G11/DoD item 5

rows.capability: GLM live verification (Z.ai credential smoke of the session tier)
rows.rationale: Doc 24 DoD gates the GLM live smoke on credential presence and records PENDING-LIVE if absent; G11 found Z.ai env unset. The GlmSessionCli code path is fake/conformance-tested but has never run against the real endpoint — per the standing live-smoke rule the adapter 'is not done' until it does.

rows.capability: GLM contractual/concurrency constraints as scheduler inputs (quota tiers, peak multipliers, ToS harness restriction)
rows.rationale: The parts the design demanded of the harness card are shipped: ceiling 1 encoded, officially-sanctioned harness (Claude Code) used, auth token never printed. The time-aware/quota-aware remainder is covered by the quota-aware-scheduling debt row.

rows.capability: Grok ACP adapter full verb set (spawn/prompt/interrupt/approve/kill native; live 8/8 E2E)
rows.rationale: impl/src/grok-acp.mjs, driver-reachable and index-exported; live E2E ledger at docs/reference/evidence/grok-0.1.216/. Includes the auth-gate typed failure, adapter-minted turn ids, single-terminal policy, and the refusal→lifecycle.crashed signal that feeds the non-refuser routing story (GA18).

rows.capability: Grok steer emulation with mandatory cancel-first ordering (queue-not-splice finding)
rows.rationale: Live probe settled the semantics (mid-turn prompts queue; cancel kills active+queued); the adapter implements GA13 cancel-then-reprompt with steerPending marker, emits control.steer{emulated:true}, and the card honestly declares steer 'emulated'. The one-turn-at-a-time guard protects against the silent-queue footgun.

rows.capability: Grok ask-user / answer() verb
rows.rationale: GA12 named gap: 'answer() unsupported on the grok ACP wire — no ask-user primitive', deliberately not emulated per D1 no-silent-emulation; carded 'unsupported'. This is documented fencing in the adapter contract, not an oversight.

rows.capability: Grok client fs/terminal capability delegation (x.ai fs/terminal server→client traffic)
rows.rationale: GA6 deliberate decline: adapter initializes with fs.readTextFile:false, writeTextFile:false, terminal:false and mcpServers:[] — 'baton deliberately delegates NO client-side fs/terminal to the worker's agent'; anything sent anyway is -32601 auto-answered observably.

rows.capability: Grok x.ai/* extension surface usage (git/worktree, search, prompt_history, compact_conversation, share_session, telemetry)
rows.rationale: 72-method catalog researched; none invoked. Baton's own worktree manager and log substrate cover the worktree/history needs; programmatic compaction could matter for long sessions but nothing consumes it. Not fenced beyond the GA6 client-delegation decline.

rows.capability: Grok multi-client attach (agent serve WebSocket, agent leader shared process)
rows.rationale: Researched with leader multiplexing semantics flagged as an open unknown; adapter uses a private stdio child per worker, which is sufficient single-box. Multi-machine attach is fenced with the remote-fleet cut; local observer attach is unfenced but low value until a monitor UI exists.

rows.capability: Grok --best-of-n parallel attempts / --check self-verification
rows.rationale: docs/22 §5 retired framings include 'best-of-N ensemble — correctly stood down'; self-verification by the worker contradicts the trust-gate principle (driver re-runs checks itself, never worker self-report).

rows.capability: Harness sandbox configuration (grok kernel profiles/GROK_SANDBOX, codex named permission profiles, claude sandbox settings)
rows.rationale: Researched in depth on all three; baton's isolation story is the git worktree + trust gate, and codex threads do get sandbox 'workspace-write'. Kernel-grade sandboxing of fleet workers is unconfigured and the grok silent-degrade-to-unenforced warning is unmonitored. Not fenced.

rows.capability: Harness version pinning / auto-update control for fleet workers
rows.rationale: Dossiers recommend disabling grok auto-update and regenerating codex schemas per release; shipped cards carry a probed or static version string but nothing pins or verifies binaries at spawn. SDK/CLI lockstep hazards documented for claude.

rows.capability: Fleet driver core loop (spawn/watch/steer/interrupt/answer/re-verify across vendors)
rows.rationale: createDriver() + Coordinator's 8 commands over three live-proven session adapters (Claude, Codex, Grok) plus GLM subclass and MockAdapter; the north-star loop exists end-to-end at driver level. Caveat: live multi-vendor capstone evidence is the doc-24 DoD; fake-backed E2E is what tests exercise.

rows.capability: AI-drives / deterministic-plumbing split
rows.rationale: The coordinator is a deterministic non-LLM program: injectable clock, no process.env reads, no model calls; dispatch/fencing/verification/event-log are exact. The orchestrating agent sits above createDriver as designed.

rows.capability: Independent verification trust gate (fresh-worktree re-run, forge-catch, claim-divergence, pinned verification)
rows.rationale: referee.verify() in a freshVerifySandbox with SameWorktreeError guard; verification command pinned from the brief at spawn; forged 'completed' yields failed (R4); claim divergence detected without trusting worker exit codes (R2). Wired as the sole done-gate via referee.accept() (C1, doc-24-verified fixed).

rows.capability: Red→green gate (acceptance test fails at base sha, passes after change)
rows.rationale: Built-but-unwired in the classic sense: referee supports opts.baseSandbox and computes redGreen, but index.refereeFn passes opts={} and never builds a base sandbox — verdict.redGreen is ALWAYS null through createDriver, so createDriver({requireRedGreen:true}) would reject every task. A headline docs/21 feature whose flag is exposed on the public API yet cannot work. No fencing text.
rows.researchedSource: docs/21 headline table; docs/23 C1 row; impl referee.mjs baseSandbox

rows.capability: Coverage-of-change gate
rows.rationale: Implemented in referee but unreachable twice over: createBrief() silently strips verification.coverageCommand, and nothing computes task.changedLines (worktree.changedLines() has no caller). requireCoverage:true is likewise a poisoned flag. Not fenced.

rows.capability: Mutation probe (plant faults in changed lines, verify tests catch them)
rows.rationale: Researched (Meta ACH basis), never started; no fencing text. Ranks below red→green/coverage since those are prerequisites in the same hardening ladder.

rows.capability: Independent oracle (different vendor writes gate tests blind from the pinned spec)
rows.rationale: Researched as the defeat of worker-grades-own-homework; absent. The E2 decorrelation EVAL is fenced to phase 11 (docs/24) but the oracle FEATURE has no fencing text; it is now buildable since the multi-vendor session fleet exists.

rows.capability: Impact-selected test re-run (regression test selection in the trust gate)
rows.rationale: Researched; the trust gate re-runs only the single pinned command, which already bounds cost for MVP briefs. No fencing text.

rows.capability: Cross-vendor review pass before the trust gate
rows.rationale: Called 'the value the whole cross-vendor premise rests on' (docs/21) and now mechanically possible with three vendors live, but no review step exists in the pipeline. Its preferred representation (semantic diff) is fenced (docs/22 §5), but a plain-diff cross-vendor review is not fenced anywhere.

rows.capability: Semantic diff, structured (syntax-aware) merge, effect tripwire
rows.rationale: docs/22 §5: 'semantic diff/merge, structured merge + effect tripwire — deferred bets.'

rows.capability: Merge/integration step + git-push approval gate (lifecycle beyond a verified branch)
rows.rationale: docs/22 §6 item 5 names these missing MVP behaviors explicitly (not deferred): the lifecycle stops at a verified baton/<taskId> branch with no merge step, and git push is not approval-gated (the irreversible-side-effect gate is absent). Of the three named items only .baton git-exclusion was fixed (doc 24 G8). Branches also accumulate (reap never deletes them). Without merge, a 'completed' fleet task still requires manual integration.

rows.capability: Delegation-contract brief (objective, scope paths, DoD, exact verification command, per-vendor rendering)
rows.rationale: createBrief()/validateBrief() (D2, deep-frozen, index-exported) + renderBrief dialects codex-v2/grok-acp + renderPrompt for claude sessions. Caveat: coordinator.spawn() accepts raw un-validated brief objects without calling validateBrief.

rows.capability: Plan-gate (worker plan approved before budget spend)
rows.rationale: docs/22 §3 records it as STUB — 'brief typedef mentions planGate, no enforcement code' — and nothing changed at HEAD; plan session/update variants from grok are even in the deliberate-ignore table. Reuses the existing question channel, so the build cost is low relative to burn-prevention value. Not fenced.
